note: Recast from the redescription of S. malaccensis by Bourguignon & Roisin (2011), the original in English; the soldier (both large and small) is described, and the alate is recorded as Unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Large soldier: body large. Head round, about as long as wide, with about 20 setae; labrum short and large; antenna usually 16 segments; pronotum large, with about 15 setae on the margins; mesonotum and metanotum with about 10 each on the posterior margin; abdomen with about 10 per segment; mandibles very large, the right mandible with a large basal boss. Measurements (mm, 6 large soldiers from 2 colonies): head length to the anterior margin of the postclypeus 1.70—2.09; head length to the labral tip 2.03—2.43; maximum head width 1.95—2.04; pronotum width 1.17—1.25; right mandible length 1.07—1.15; minimum postmentum width 0.26—0.34; hind tibia length 1.54—1.64.

Small soldier: head with 5—10 setae; labrum moderately elongate, almost reaching the mandibular tips; postclypeus short and wide; antenna 15 or 16 segments; pronotum with about 10 setae on the margins; mesonotum and metanotum with about 8 each on the posterior margin; mandibles slender, marginal teeth short. Measurements (mm, 1 individual from the type colony; in parentheses 6 small soldiers from 2 colonies): head length to the anterior margin of the postclypeus 1.28 (1.01—1.22); head length to the labral tip 1.77 (1.52—1.78); maximum head width 1.00 (0.81—0.95); pronotum length 0.50 (0.37—0.49); pronotum width 0.70 (0.59—0.73); right mandible length 0.85 (0.72—0.87); maximum postmentum width 0.36 (0.30—0.35); hind tibia length 1.18 (1.03—1.14).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: It differs from the other New Guinea species by the large, round head and the stout mandibles of the large soldier. The alate is not known. In New Guinea it has been collected only twice, in the northwest, in Papua; the species is widespread in the Sunda region.
